title: All-on-X Recovery: Timeline, Pain, Diet, and Aftercare
seoTitle: All-on-X Recovery Timeline: Pain, Diet and Aftercare
seoDescription: What All-on-X recovery looks like week by week, from swelling and soft foods to your final teeth. Plan your healing with our Valencia team.
excerpt: A day-by-day look at All-on-X healing: when swelling peaks, what to eat, when to return to work, and the warning signs that mean you should call.
keyTakeaways: Soreness and swelling usually peak on days 2 to 4 and ease to mild discomfort within one to two weeks.
Expect a soft diet for at least two weeks; hard or crunchy foods wait until your clinician clears you.
Many patients return to desk work within 5 to 10 days; heavy exercise waits two to four weeks.
Implants integrate over three to six months before the final prosthesis is made and fitted.
Fever above 101.5 F, spreading redness, heavy bleeding or a loose implant mean you should call right away.
imageAlt: Smiling patient in the treatment chair with a dentist and a panoramic X-ray behind him
flags: Pain evidence is borrowed from forum posts about gum grafting and a frenectomy, then presented as what All-on-X patients experience; weak relevance.
Reddit anecdotes (weight loss, cardio at day 5) are blended with clinical guidance throughout; consider trimming.
Implant survival 'above 90 percent at five to ten years' is cited to PMC4647895; the same link is reused across several posts for different claims and is unverified.
FAQ 5 answer in the faq data ends with stray CTA text 'Request Your Post-Op Guide'.
First 24 hours tip says to 'take prescribed antibiotics' as routine; antibiotics are not always prescribed.
